true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) version

Ruby has no method overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. The first definition is dead code, and Ruby emits a 'method redefined' warning. Any existing caller using the width/height form now breaks: with five arguments it raises ArgumentError, and with four arguments the height is bound to `opts`, so `opts[:allow_animation]` raises or misbehaves. Keep a single `downsize` signature and update every caller, or give the new variant a different name.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb

`maxSizeKB` was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and is now a constant 10MB for both images and attachments. Attachments are no longer checked against `max_attachment_size_kb` on the client. A site with a smaller limit lets users upload up to 10MB before the server rejects it. A site with a larger limit blocks files between the configured limit and 10MB ... and anything above 10MB, even though the setting allows it. The error dialog also reports 10MB instead of the real limit. The same hard-coded value is repeated in the 413 handler at line 246. A shared constant would at least avoid the duplication.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage dimensions break the animated GIF downsize path, so the loop silently fails

The call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` with the dimension string "80%". When the setting is on and the filename matches /\.GIF$/i, `optimize` switches to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That delegates to the gifsicle command `--resize-fit 80%`, and gifsicle's `--resize-fit` takes WxH, not a percentage. The command fails and `convert_with` returns false. The return value is ignored, so the loop runs all 5 attempts, spawning a process each time, and the oversized GIF is passed on unchanged. There is also no check or log that downsizing failed.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Size check relies on the Tempfile handle after the file is rewritten externally by convert/ImageOptim

`OptimizedImage.downsize` rewrites the file through its path using external `convert` and ImageOptim. The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` depend on `tempfile.size`. If ImageOptim replaces the file (new inode) rather than rewriting it in place, the open Tempfile handle can report a stale size or read stale content. The loop would then keep downsizing needlessly, or the recorded filesize would not match the stored data. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` and reopen or rewind the file after modifying it.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL download limit changed from the site setting to a hard-coded 10MB

`FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` became `10.megabytes`. The download cap no longer follows site configuration. Sites that set `max_image_size_kb` lower now fetch up to 10MB of arbitrary data before it is rejected or downsized. Non-image attachments get the same fixed cap regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`. This should be a named constant or setting.

New auto-downsizing behaviour and signature change have no tests

The PR adds a retry loop that rewrites the user's uploaded file, a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature, and removes setting-based limits from the JS validators. It adds or updates no specs. Untested cases include an oversized image being shrunk below the limit, the 5-attempt cap, GIF handling, and `max_image_size_kb == 0`. The existing JS utilities tests that exercised the setting-based limits are also not updated. The duplicate `downsize` definition would have been caught by a simple spec.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation calls `sub!` on a possibly-nil host

`self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil, for example `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or a POST to the controller without `embeddable_host[host]`. The user gets a 500 instead of a validation error. The `sub!` calls also mutate the caller's string in place. Guard with `host.present?` or use non-destructive `sub`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy dereference a nil record for unknown ids

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing or already-deleted id. `destroy` then calls `nil.destroy`, and `update` passes nil to `save_host`, which calls `nil.host=`. Both raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Double-clicking delete or a stale admin page hits this. Use `find` and let Discourse's RecordNotFound handling return a 404, or add an explicit not-found check. A missing `params[:embeddable_host]` has the same effect in `save_host`.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hosts with a port (or uppercase) can be saved but never match

The validation regex explicitly allows `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the normalizer keeps the port. But `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so a host like `example.com:8080` is accepted and then never matches any referer. The right-hand side is also not downcased, so a mixed-case referer or embed URL fails against the lowercased column. Either reject ports on save or compare against `host:port`, and downcase the lookup value.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL unescaped

Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`. The migration inserts each line with raw SQL, so the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path never runs. Rows keep the `http://` prefix (and `\r` or whitespace if the setting had it), and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so they never match. Every existing site that used the scheme form silently loses embedding after upgrade. The value is also interpolated as `'#{h}'` with no quoting or escaping, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration, or injects SQL. Strip scheme, path and whitespace in Ruby and use `quote`/sanitization.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files

`category_fabricator.rb` now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. All the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. It works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but it looks like an accidental swap. Anyone searching for the category fabricator or the embeddable host one will look in the wrong file, and the diff of both files is misleading. Restore the category fabricators to `category_fabricator.rb` and put only the embeddable_host fabricator in its own file.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL unescaped

Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`. The migration inserts each line with raw SQL, so the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path never runs. Rows keep the `http://` prefix (and `\r` or whitespace if the setting had it), and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so they never match. Every existing site that used the scheme form silently loses embedding after upgrade. The value is also interpolated as `'#{h}'` with no quoting or escaping, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration, or injects SQL. Strip scheme, path and whitespace in Ruby and use `quote`/sanitization.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when no `embed_category` row exists

`execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns a row. `site_settings` only stores rows for settings an admin changed. On a fresh install, or any site that never set `embed_category`, the result set is empty, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem: `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id` also breaks if that row is not present yet. Check for an empty result before indexing and default to a safe category id.

false_positives.candidate:
"is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests what it says

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for any embeddable host. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic. It would still pass if host handling were broken. The behavior change (expandable posts no longer require a configured host) is untested, and the test name is misleading. Remove the case or rewrite it to reflect the actual condition.

New admin controllers have no behavioral tests

Both new controller specs only assert that the class inherits from `AdminController`. Nothing tests create/update/destroy of hosts, the uncategorized default, validation error rendering, non-staff access being denied, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-record and nil-host crashes in this PR would have been caught by such tests. `embeddable_host_spec` also lacks cases for nil host, ports, case and duplicates.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for the topic, and the next line calls `tu.notification_level` on it. That raises NoMethodError and the page returns a 500. The URL is a plain GET, so any logged-in user can reach it for a topic they never visited, for example by following a forwarded email link from another account. Handle nil, either with `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row, or by returning a clean error.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and MessageBus

The notification level is set by assigning the attribute and calling `tu.save!`. Everywhere else it is changed through `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (to `user_changed`) and publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus. Here the reason stays at its old value, the timestamp is not updated, and other open tabs are not told about the change. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` to keep behaviour consistent.

New unsubscribe feature has no tests

The only spec change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing fixture so it stops raising. Nothing asserts that the per-topic URL appears in the email body or HTML part. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, covering downgrade to regular, escalation to muted, the slug redirect, the missing-TopicUser case and the not-logged-in case. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. The behaviour problems above (nil TopicUser, non-idempotent toggle) would have been caught by basic controller tests.

State-changing action exposed on GET (CSRF / prefetch)

`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` map to an action that writes `topic_users.notification_level`. GET requests are not covered by CSRF protection. A post or any third-party page that embeds an image or link pointing at `/t/x/<id>/unsubscribe` will change the notification level for any logged-in viewer. Link prefetchers and scanners trigger it too. The write should be a POST/PUT from the client page (with a CSRF token) after the user confirms, rather than a side effect of loading the page.

Template name likely does not match the topicUnsubscribe route

The route is declared as `topicUnsubscribe` and the controller, view and route files are all named `topic-unsubscribe`, but the template lives at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, so its name is `topic/unsubscribe`. The Discourse resolver looks up `topicUnsubscribe`, `topic_unsubscribe` and `topic-unsubscribe`, not `topic/unsubscribe`. If it does not resolve, the unsubscribe page renders empty and shows neither the message nor the notification dropdown. Rename the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`, or verify that the resolver finds the nested path.

Unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent: reloading the page mutes the topic

The first visit drops a watching or tracking user to regular. Any later hit on the same URL, whether a page reload, a double click, or an email-client or security-scanner prefetch, sees `notification_level <= regular` and mutes the topic. A user who only asked to stop watching can end up with the topic fully muted. The resulting state depends on how many times the URL is requested, not on user intent. The action should be idempotent, or require explicit confirmation before escalating to muted.

add_unsubscribe_link now silently requires an unsubscribe_url option

The English `unsubscribe_link` string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) interpolate it from `template_args` with no default. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`, including plugins and other mailers, will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the email is built. The spec had to be edited to pass `unsubscribe_url` to avoid this. Provide a fallback in `template_args`, or only include the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which writes to the DB, so stats are counted more than once per signup

`should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from inside a validator, which should be side-effect free. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again, so one signup attempt bumps the counters at least twice. Any other `valid?` call on a user with a changed email does the same. Statistics for `do_nothing` entries are inflated. Entries for `block` can be written outside the save transaction, so they are not rolled back. The lookup-and-record-hit logic should run once at a deliberate point, or the validator should do a read-only check.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized, so it is trivially bypassed

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact string match, and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` is case-sensitive too. If `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked, `Bad@SpamClub.com` or ` bad@spamclub.com` passes the check. The rest of the codebase normalizes emails with `Email.downcase` and `strip`. Stored and queried emails should be normalized (for example downcased on save and on lookup), otherwise the blocking feature is easy to evade.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Array literal on the controller prototype is shared across instances

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared in `extend({...})`, so the one array lives on the prototype and is shared by every instance. `pushObject` then mutates shared state, so rejected emails persist across all controller instances (and across tests). It should be initialized per instance in `init`, for example `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`.

Client marks any email-error rejection as 'invalid' and hides the real server reason

The JS adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `errors.email` is present, and `emailValidation` then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` text. The server-side reasons (`blocked`, `not_allowed`, already taken) are not shown in the field. The new `user.email.blocked` message appears only in the flash, and the inline field gives a misleading "invalid" message. The per-field error from `errors.email` should be used as the validation reason.

Invalid computed-property dependent key 'rejectedEmails.@each'

In Ember, `@each` must be followed by a property name (`rejectedEmails.@each.foo`). To observe array membership changes the key should be `rejectedEmails.[]`. With a bare `.@each` the `emailValidation` property may not be invalidated when `pushObject` adds a rejected email. The "rejected email" feedback then wouldn't update until `accountEmail` changes.

Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses updates under concurrency

`record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the row, increments in Ruby and writes back the absolute value. Two concurrent signups with the same email both read N and both write N+1, so a hit is lost. It also runs a full save with callbacks and a uniqueness validation query on every check. Use `BlockedEmail.increment_counter(:match_count, record.id)` or `update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` so the increment happens atomically in SQL.

Tests don't cover validator interaction with whitelist/blacklist or the User model integration

The spec only stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and checks the error toggles. It does not cover the moved whitelist/blacklist logic, the short-circuit when an earlier error exists, a nil or blank value, or an end-to-end `User` validation. It also does not cover the new `errors`/`values` JSON returned by `UsersController#create`, or the repeated validation calls that inflate `match_count`. Regressions in the refactor out of `User#email_validator` would not be caught here.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open on a URL string allows command execution and unchecked fetches

`open(url)` is `Kernel#open` with open-uri loaded, so a string starting with `|` runs a shell command. `import_remote` does not validate its argument itself. Only the `TopicRetriever` path checks the host. The Disqus thor task passes `t[:link]` straight from an XML export, and `PollFeed` does `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` the same way. Use `URI.parse(url).open`, or RestClient, after verifying the scheme is http or https, and set explicit timeouts. `open-uri` is also only required in `poll_feed.rb`, so `import_remote` can fail with ENOENT if that file has not been loaded.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring match

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. Any origin that is a substring of the configured URL passes. For example, with `discourseUrl = 'http://forum.example.com/'`, a message from origin `http://forum.example.co` is accepted. Compare `e.origin` for equality against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Request referer interpolated into an inline JS string as the targetOrigin

`request.referer` is attacker-influenced (path and query are free-form) and is only HTML-escaped inside a `<script>` block, where entities are not decoded. A trailing backslash in the referer escapes the closing quote and breaks the script, so the resize message is never sent. HTML-escaping is also the wrong encoding for a JS context, and `&` sequences end up in the string. `postMessage` expects an origin, so emit `scheme://host[:port]` derived server-side and serialize it with `to_json` or `j`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: import mutates its input and interpolates the URL into HTML unescaped `contents << ...` appends the footer to the caller's string in place. Callers that reuse the string, such as the memoized `let(:contents)` in the spec, see it change. The URL is also placed into `#{url}` without escaping. The only validation is `/^https?:\/\//`, which uses `^` rather than `\A`, so a multi-line value with `http://` on a later line passes. A `'` or `<` in the URL can inject attributes or markup into a post that is never sanitized. Build a new string, escape the URL, and anchor the regex with `\A`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby and breaks the best template

The `if/else` opened on line 2 is closed with `end if`, a modifier `if` with no condition. Erubis appends `;` after a statement tag, which yields `end if ;`. That is a syntax error, or at best an `if` conditioned on the next emitted output statement. Either way the template cannot render correctly, so `embed/best` fails whenever a topic already exists. It should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs do not render views, so nothing catches this.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One bad feed item aborts the whole poll (nil content, no per-item rescue)

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`, which is common for RSS 2.0 feeds that only carry `description`. The loop has no per-item rescue, so one such item, or an exception from `TopicEmbed.import` (such as `create!` validation or a DB error on a long title), stops the import of every item after it. The job runs with `retry: false`, so the same item blocks the feed on every hourly run. Fall back to `description` when `content` is nil, and rescue and log errors per item.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Request referer interpolated into an inline JS string as the targetOrigin

`request.referer` is attacker-influenced (path and query are free-form) and is only HTML-escaped inside a `<script>` block, where entities are not decoded. A trailing backslash in the referer escapes the closing quote and breaks the script, so the resize message is never sent. HTML-escaping is also the wrong encoding for a JS context, and `&` sequences end up in the string. `postMessage` expects an origin, so emit `scheme://host[:port]` derived server-side and serialize it with `to_json` or `j`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Controller specs pass for the wrong reason and miss the key access check

'is 404 without an embed_url' does not set `embeddable_host`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess before `params.require` is reached. The test passes without exercising the missing-parameter path. `should_not be_success` is also too weak to tell the cases apart. There is no test for a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host`, which is the central security check, and none for a malformed referer. Nothing covers the `loading` branch.

Disqus import silently drops the --category option and original thread dates

The `-c/--category` option and its lookup are removed, and topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which takes no category or `created_at`. Existing users of the task lose category placement and the original topic timestamps. Each import now also performs a live HTTP fetch of the thread link, so the task fails or produces content from the live site if the link is dead. This is a behaviour change unrelated to the embed feature and is not mentioned in the PR.

Failed post creation is not detected before creating the TopicEmbed

`PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when it failed and rolled back, for example on host-spam detection or a save failure. That post is unsaved, so `post.present?` is still true. `TopicEmbed.create!` then runs with `post_id: nil` and `topic_id: nil`, which raises a NOT NULL violation. This surfaces as a confusing exception in the job instead of a clean failure. The guard should check `post.persisted?` or `post.errors.blank?`. The update branch has a related problem: `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted, and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then blows up.

New gems added to the Gemfile but only the rails4 lockfile was updated

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added for both Rails 3 and Rails 4 boot modes, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was updated. If a separate `Gemfile.lock` exists for the Rails 3 mode, it is now out of sync, and `bundle install --deployment` or frozen installs there will fail.

Throttle is keyed on the full URL and non-atomic, so it is trivially bypassed

The key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so varying the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) on the allowed host gets a fresh throttle slot each time. Each one triggers a full `Jobs::PollFeed` run (fetch, parse and import of the whole feed) when feed polling is enabled, plus a remote HTTP fetch and a new topic via `import_remote`. This allows request amplification and duplicate topics per URL variant. The embed URL should be canonicalized, and there should be a global limit on retrievals. Separately, `setnx` followed by `expire` is not atomic. A crash between the two leaves a key that never expires and blocks that URL permanently. Use `SET key val NX EX 60`.

Wrapping PostCreator in Topic.transaction defeats its after-commit job enqueueing

`PostCreator#create` deliberately enqueues `process_post` and `feature_topic_users` after its own transaction commits (see the comment in `enqueue_jobs`). Wrapping the call in an outer `Topic.transaction` means those jobs are enqueued before the outer transaction commits, which now also includes `TopicEmbed.create!`. In production a Sidekiq worker can pick up `process_post` before the post row is visible and fail or skip processing. It also makes the rollback semantics unclear, because the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside PostCreator's nested transaction does not roll back the outer one.

`create_table ..., force: true` runs `DROP TABLE` first if the table exists. Here it is in the new `topic_embeds` migration and in the edited `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`. The latter is an already-applied migration unrelated to this feature, and the edit has no effect except when the migration is re-run, when it silently destroys data. Remove `force: true` from the new migration and leave the old migration untouched.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores other relative forms

`href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative links such as `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, giving `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is a broken link. The same happens for `img src` on line 71. Relative paths without a leading slash (`images/a.png`, `../a.png`) are left untouched, and the code resolves against only scheme and host rather than the article URL. The port check (`!= 80 && != 443`) is also wrong for https on 80 or http on 443. `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these correctly.

`Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, so none of the normal cooking or sanitizing pipeline runs. The content comes from remote sources. In `PollFeed` it is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`, which turns escaped entities such as `<script>` back into live markup. In `import_remote` it is the readability output. Nothing in `TopicEmbed.import` or `absolutize_urls` strips scripts, event handlers, or `javascript:` links. The result is written to `posts.cooked`, shown on the main site, and emitted via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed iframe, which is served from the Discourse origin with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. A compromised or malicious feed or page can therefore run script in Discourse's origin. The imported HTML should be sanitized with a whitelist before it is saved or served.

Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

The template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the nil case, but the intended contract (omit the attribute when there is no website) is not enforced. Rename it to `include_website_name?`. false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Every fallback lookup reads SiteSetting and allocates a new array

`FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called by the I18n Fallbacks backend on every `translate_no_cache` call. Each call evaluates `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and builds and de-duplicates a new array. This sits on the hot translation path that the accelerator exists to speed up. Because `[]` is overridden to always compute, nothing is memoized. It also makes translation depend on `SiteSetting` being available, which can fail early in boot or in rake tasks before the DB is ready. A `locale` passed as a String is not de-duplicated against the Symbols in the list.

Fallback locales are only preloaded in the controller before_filter

Translations are loaded on demand. `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`, so the fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by this `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that does not go through this filter has no fallback data loaded. That includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers, `I18n.with_locale` blocks and rake tasks. If a key is missing in the user's locale, the fallback chain [locale, default, :en] finds nothing because :en may not be loaded in that process. The result is a 'translation missing: ...' string, not the English text. A fresh worker process hits this on its first email in a non-English locale. The loading belongs in the accelerator, for example `translate`/`load_locale` loading the whole fallback chain, not in one controller filter.

No tests for the new fallback behavior

The PR adds a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and a hook in `set_locale`. It also removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the production configs, which makes fallbacks active in every environment, including test and development. No spec covers any of this. Missing coverage includes: a key missing in the user locale falling back to the site default and then English, ordering and de-duplication of the chain, loading of fallback locales on demand, and interaction with the translation cache. Regressions in this globally applied behavior would go unnoticed.

Translation LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain and caches missing-translation results

The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With this PR the result also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the custom fallback chain) and on which fallback locales are already loaded. Two consequences follow. (1) If an admin changes the default locale, entries cached for other locales still hold text from the old fallback until they are evicted or the process restarts. (2) If a lookup runs before the fallback locales are loaded, the frozen 'translation missing' string is stored under that key. It is then served on every later call, even after :en has been loaded. The key should include the fallback chain, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes. Missing-translation results should not be cached.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key copies the integer Paginator logic and crashes on datetime ordering

The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`, which is a `datetime`. That raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result, so any `?optimized_pagination=true` request with at least one row returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw cursor value instead of converting the timestamp back to a datetime, as `DateTimePaginator` does. On later pages the WHERE clause would then compare the datetime column to a raw integer. The new path has to reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s conversion (`strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier`) to work at all.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Behavior change in shared BasePaginator.get_result with a misleading comment

`BasePaginator.get_result` is used by many endpoints, and this edit changes it. Non-prev cursors with a negative offset are now silently clamped to 0, so a malformed cursor returns the first page instead of failing. Prev cursors still pass the negative offset straight to the queryset, which fails, so the claim that this 'allows negative offsets' and that the queryset 'will handle boundary conditions' is false. `offset` and `start_offset` now differ in the non-prev case, but the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses `offset`. The change is unrelated to the audit log feature, risks regressions elsewhere, and should be reverted or properly validated (reject negative offsets with a `BadPaginationError`).

Comment claims negative offsets are supported but no code change backs it

The added comment says the `Cursor` constructor now 'allows negative offsets ... for efficient reverse pagination'. The constructor is unchanged (`int(offset)` already accepted negatives) and nothing downstream supports negative offsets. The comment misleads future maintainers about a capability that does not exist.

No tests for the new paginator or the new endpoint branch

The PR adds a new paginator, a new query-param-gated code path and a change to the shared `BasePaginator`, with no tests. A basic test of `?optimized_pagination=true` would have exposed the datetime `get_item_key` crash, and a negative-offset cursor test would have exposed the slicing error. There is also no coverage of the permission gating (superuser, global access, no member).

OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale; the 'else' branch is identical to the base

The class copy-pastes the whole of `get_result`. Only the negative-offset branch differs, and that branch cannot work (see the negative-slicing finding). The `else` branch is identical to the modified base logic. The result is two parallel implementations that can drift apart. The docstring's claims of 'optimized query path' and 'streamlined boundary condition handling' are not backed by any code, since the query is the same as the base class's.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset slicing is unsupported by Django and the comments claim otherwise

The code does `queryset[cursor.offset : stop]` with a negative `cursor.offset`, and the comment says "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically". Django querysets raise on negative indexing ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so a client-supplied cursor such as `value:-5:0` produces a 500. The comments ("access data beyond normal pagination bounds", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") describe a capability that does not exist. They also invite a future change to bypass offset validation. Nothing validates or bounds the user-controlled offset.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Shared BasePaginator behavior changed for every consumer with a misleading rationale

`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently changes `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is used by many endpoints. A negative offset on a forward cursor used to fail; it is now silently clamped to 0, so a malformed cursor returns the first page instead of an error. For `is_prev`, negative offsets still reach `queryset[...]` and still crash. The later trim logic (`len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) still uses the unclamped `offset`, so it is inconsistent with the actual slice. The comment says the queryset "will handle boundary conditions", which is false. This change is unrelated to the spans buffer work in the PR title.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime key used by the audit log endpoint

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw `cursor.value`. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `getattr` returns a `datetime` and `math.floor` raises `TypeError`. `DateTimePaginator` avoids this by converting through `strftime` with a multiplier and rebuilding a datetime from the cursor. Even if the key function worked, `build_queryset` would compare the `datetime` column to a raw millisecond integer. Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row will therefore 500, or produce an invalid SQL comparison on the next page.

true_positives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Eager evaluation of `organization_context.member.has_global_access` can crash every request

`enable_advanced` is computed on every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not set, as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be `None` (for example for org auth tokens or API keys with org:write that are not tied to a member). For such callers the existing audit-log endpoint now raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500, even though they never asked for the new feature. The check also uses `is_superuser` rather than `is_active_superuser`, so it ignores whether the superuser session is actually active. The new option should be evaluated lazily and `None`-safely, or not added at all.

false_positives.candidate:
Comment claims Cursor allows negative offsets for 'efficient reverse pagination', but nothing changed

The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination and enable efficient reverse pagination. `Cursor.__init__` still does `int(offset)` exactly as before, and downstream code cannot execute negative offsets (Django rejects negative slicing). The comment is misleading and documents a feature that is not implemented.

Eviction silently drops spans with a hard-coded limit and no signal

When a segment has more than 1000 spans, `zpopmin` silently discards the earliest-ending ones. The old behavior logged an error and bumped the `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric. The new path emits nothing, so truncated segments are invisible. The limit 1000 is hard-coded in Lua while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still a constructor argument that is no longer used anywhere, so configuration and behavior have diverged. Also, `zunionstore` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so a payload present in both sets (for example after a redelivery) gets its score added together. That distorts the eviction ordering, and `AGGREGATE MAX` or `MIN` would be correct.

No test covers the new eviction behavior or the new paginator/endpoint path

The tests only add the `end_timestamp_precise` argument to existing Span constructions. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans and checks that the lowest-score spans are evicted. There is none for eviction after a merge via `zunionstore` either, and none for the removal of the `max_segment_spans` check in `_load_segment_data`. There are also no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, for the `optimized_pagination=true` branch of the audit-log endpoint, or for the paginator offset-clamping change. The new paginator and endpoint code would fail on first use (datetime key handling, negative slicing).

Redirect-chain depth limit silently cut from 10000 to 1000

The loop bound changed from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, and the comment documenting the limitation was deleted. This is unrelated to the eviction work and is not mentioned in the PR. Span trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now stop resolving early. The span is then attached to an intermediate set instead of the real segment, which fragments segments. The reduction should be justified or reverted.

Switching key type from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight segments during deploy

Segment keys (`span-buf:s:*`) change from sets (`sadd`/`sscan`/`scard`/`sunionstore`) to sorted sets (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zcard`/`zunionstore`) with no migration or versioned key prefix. Keys written by old consumers live up to `redis_ttl` (1h). Any new consumer touching an existing set-typed key, in `zadd`, in the Lua `zcard`/`zunionstore`, or in `zscan` on flush, gets a `WRONGTYPE` error. That fails the batch or the flusher and can crash-loop the consumer until the old keys expire or are flushed. A new key prefix, or a drain-before-deploy step, is needed.

true_positives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blanket exception swallowing in test factory helper hides malformed fixtures

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the float conversion in `except Exception: pass`. A malformed `client_sample_rate` (for example a string) is silently ignored and the event is stored without `sample_rate`. The upsampling tests then fail on count assertions rather than at the real cause. The `if client_sample_rate:` check also skips a legitimate rate of 0. Narrow the exceptions or let invalid fixtures fail loudly.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache layer is unnecessary, collision-prone, and never invalidated

The allowlist check is an in-process `options.get` followed by an `in` scan. Wrapping it in `cache.get`/`cache.set` (a network round-trip to memcached or redis) is likely slower than the lookup it replaces. It also adds staleness: option changes take up to 60s to apply, and the module's own `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere. The key is built from `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash, so two different project sets can collide and share an eligibility result. It is also not independent of the organization's data beyond org id. Joining the sorted ids, or dropping the cache entirely, would be safer.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling check uses the outer `dataset` and request query instead of the scoped dataset and actual query

`_get_event_stats` takes `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check passes the closed-over endpoint-level `dataset`. The check also reads `request.GET['query']` instead of the `query` argument. In the dashboard-widget split path, the code calls `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction")` or `scoped_dataset` with a modified query. The decision is still based on the original dataset (for example `metrics_enhanced_performance`, which returns False) and the original request string. The same widget can then get upsampled counts in one branch and raw counts in another. The split-decision logic compares `error_results` against `original_results`, which can come out inconsistent. The decision should be computed from `scoped_dataset` and the `query` actually being executed.

false_positives.candidate:
Docstring contradicts the caching behavior

The NOTE on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says it reads the allowlist fresh each time so the latest configuration is always used. The caller wraps it in a 60-second cache, so results can be up to a minute stale. Comments in the endpoint make similar claims ("cached result ensures consistent behavior", "most current schema assumptions", "better query optimization and caching") that are not true of the code. They will mislead maintainers about when the allowlist takes effect.

Endpoint tests miss top_events, negated queries, the cache path and the dashboard split path

The new tests only cover plain timeseries with `count()`. They do not cover the `topEvents` branch where the transform is also applied. They do not cover `!event.type:error` or compound queries, which the substring check mishandles. They do not cover events with NULL `sample_weight`, the likely failure for `sum(sample_weight)`. They do not cover the dashboard split path, where the outer `dataset` is used instead of the scoped one. The tests also mock `options` while using the real cache, and `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` have no direct unit tests. The 60s cache and the unused invalidation are therefore untested.

Stray submodule gitlink committed to the repository

A new `sentry-repo` entry is added as a git submodule pointer (`Subproject commit a5d2909...`, the base commit). It is unrelated to the feature and has no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, so it looks like an accidental commit of a local checkout. It can break `git submodule` operations and should be removed from the PR.

Substring match on 'event.type:error' misclassifies negated and compound queries

`_is_error_focused_query` returns True if the raw lowercase query string contains `event.type:error`. That matches `!event.type:error` (the opposite intent), `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and any query where the text appears inside a longer token or value. In those cases `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over transaction or other non-error rows, which have no sample weight. The result is wrong counts or Snuba errors. The docstring claims this errs on the side of caution, but a substring match does the opposite. It needs to parse the query, or at least check token boundaries and negation.

Upsampling transform applied in RPC branches that can never be eligible

`use_rpc` is only true for `spans_rpc` and `ourlogs`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for every dataset other than errors and discover, so `upsampling_enabled` is always False in the two RPC branches (top-events and timeseries). The `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` calls there are dead code. They also suggest to readers that RPC datasets are supported, and they would feed a non-RPC `upsampled_count() as count` column into the RPC `y_axes` if the gating ever changed.

upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) with no NULL handling

The new aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Events stored before `sample_weight` was populated, or without a client sample rate, have NULL in that column. `sum` skips NULLs, so those events are counted as 0, or the whole bucket becomes NULL and `toInt64` then yields 0 or an error. Allowlisted projects therefore show undercounted or zeroed error charts as soon as their data contains any unweighted events. The comment says the schema guarantees the column exists, but a nullable column existing does not mean it is populated. It should be `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` so unweighted events count as 1. Also, the function is registered as a public (non-private) discover function. Users can call `upsampled_count()` directly, including on datasets or event types where `sample_weight` does not exist.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty columns and data

When the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is on, every table widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. The real `result.data` / `result.meta`, field aliases, loading state and custom field renderers are all ignored. Any org with the flag enabled sees every dashboard table widget as an empty table. If this is intentional scaffolding, it should be marked clearly. Otherwise pass `result.data`/`result.meta` (converted to `TabularData`) and the columns.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness and is not enforced when both are missing

`validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use `self.initial_data.get(...)` truthiness, so a value of `0` (valid for both `age` and `timestamp`) is treated as absent. A report with `age: 0` and `timestamp: 5` therefore passes. Field-level validators also only run when the field is present, so a report containing neither `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted, although the comments say exactly one spec format is required. Use `is not None` / `in initial_data` checks and add an object-level `validate()` requiring exactly one of the two.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check. Requests from orgs without the feature (which get a 404) are still counted as assemble API usage, which skews the metric. Also, `request.user.id` is None for org-auth-token requests, so those events carry no user. Move the call after the feature check unless counting rejected requests is intended.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

false_positives.candidate:
60s processing deadline for a batch of up to 100 external identity refreshes

`check_auth_identities` loops over up to `chunk_size=100` auth identities. Each `check_single_auth_identity` makes a network call to the SSO provider's `refresh_identity`. A fixed `processing_deadline_duration=60` allows only about 0.6s per identity, so a slow provider can hit the deadline. `check_auth` has already bumped `last_synced` for the whole chunk, so the identities that were not reached will not be re-selected until the next interval (about a day). The final `check_auth.apply_async` reschedule is also skipped. Size the deadline to the chunk, or reduce the chunk size.

Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'

`DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` and the `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` project option default both change from `"low"` to `"off"`. Every project that never set the option explicitly changes behaviour on deploy: autofix automation turns off, and the API/serializer now reports `off`. This has nothing to do with the PR title (replay bulk delete), and the PR description is just 'Test 5'. It should be a separate, clearly described change, with a decision on whether existing projects need a migration to preserve their effective setting.

Error timestamps (seconds) compared against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)

`gen_request_data` interleaves errors with breadcrumbs by checking `error_events[idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp comes from the nodestore event payload, which is epoch seconds. The `event["timestamp"]` from an rrweb replay segment is normally epoch milliseconds. With real data every error then compares as 'earlier' than the first replay event, so all errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. The Seer summary receives a wrong timeline. The tests use the same unit for both sides (`now.timestamp()` for both, and small numbers in `test_get_request_data`), so they cannot catch this. Normalise the units, for example by multiplying the error timestamp by 1000, and add a test that uses millisecond replay timestamps.

Issue title placed unescaped inside markdown link text and truncated mid-token

`MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` puts the raw (user-controlled) issue title inside `[**{title}**]({url})`. A title containing `]`, `[`, `**` or `](...)` breaks the link or lets the title alter the rendered link in the PR comment. `_truncate_title` cuts at 50 characters without regard to markdown, so it can also leave an unbalanced `**` or bracket and mangle the rest of the comment. The title should be escaped, or have markdown-significant characters stripped, before it is interpolated.

New max_segment_id=None handling is not actually exercised

The test now feeds `max_segment_id: None`, but it patches `delete_matched_rows`, so the real `_make_recording_filenames` / `delete_replay_recordings` code that gained the `None` early-return is never run. A regression back to `range(None + 1)` would still pass. Add a direct unit test of `_make_recording_filenames` with a `None` segment id, or an unmocked `delete_matched_rows` test.

Per-issue get_recommended_event() lookup when building PR comments

`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue in the comment (up to 5). That performs an event lookup (Snuba plus nodestore) per issue, synchronously in the comment-building path, just to show an environment name. Failures are swallowed and logged only at `info`, so persistent lookup problems will go unnoticed and the comment silently loses the environment. Consider a single batched lookup, or reading the environment from data already available on the group or query.

Query key omits organization; isLoading/attributes semantics changed

The react-query key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, but `queryOptions` contains no organization slug, and the fetch URL does depend on `organization.slug`. Cached attribute keys can be reused across organizations within a session. The hook also now returns `isLoading: isFetching`, which is true on every background refetch rather than only the initial load. `attributes` can now be `undefined` (it was previously always a `TagCollection`). Callers that gate UI on `isLoading` or assume a defined object may flicker or break. The old `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false` options were also dropped.

Saved queries with multi-yAxis visualizes will always look modified

A Visualize now holds a single yAxis. A saved query stored in the old format `{yAxes: [a, b]}` is parsed into two Visualizes, which `toJSON()` serialises as `[{yAxes:[a]},{yAxes:[b]}]`. `valueIsEqual(visualizes.map(v => v.toJSON()), singleQuery?.visualize, true)` then never matches the stored value. The Save button is permanently highlighted as 'has changes', and the saved overlay is split into separate charts. There is no migration or normalisation of the stored `visualize` shape on load.

Unknown report types reject the whole batch with 422

`type` is a `ChoiceField` limited to 8 values, and a single invalid report makes the endpoint return 422 for the entire array. The Reporting API can deliver other report types to a collector (e.g. `network-error` or newer types), and browsers batch reports. One report of an unlisted type discards all valid reports in the same request. The previous code only used the types as hints and accepted everything. For a data-collection endpoint it is safer to skip or tag unknown types than to fail the batch.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write

The code reads the encrypted blob, finds the index, nulls the entry, re-encrypts and writes the whole blob back, with no lock or compare-and-swap. Two concurrent logins using the same single-use code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write lands. Both then succeed, violating the "can be used exactly once" guarantee. Concurrent logins using different codes can also overwrite each other's update and resurrect a used code. Use a transaction or optimistic concurrency, for example update where `backupCodes` equals the value that was read.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
"missing_backup_codes" message points to a settings feature that does not exist

Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. When they click "Lost access" they get "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." There is no UI or endpoint to generate or regenerate backup codes for an already-enabled account. The only way to get codes is to disable 2FA, which requires a TOTP code or backup code they no longer have. The message gives an impossible instruction. Either add a regenerate flow or change the message to something actionable.

Backup-code login can skip password verification by also sending a dummy totpCode

The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121, unchanged). The new branch at line 131 is chosen when `credentials.backupCode` is present, and it never looks at `totpCode`. An attacker can send `email` + any non-empty `totpCode` + a valid `backupCode`. The password check is skipped and the backup-code branch authenticates the request. A single secret (a 40-bit backup code) then replaces both password and second factor. The PR adds a new credential path on top of this guard without tightening it. Fix: always verify the password for CAL-provider users when no external TOTP/JWT flow is in progress, and make the backup-code branch independent of `totpCode`.

Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable/resetState

2FA is already enabled server-side once the TOTP code is verified, but `onEnable()` and `resetState()` now run only from the "Close" button on the DisplayBackupCodes step. The Cancel button is hidden there. If the user dismisses the dialog via Escape, the overlay or the X (`onOpenChange`), the parent is never told 2FA was enabled, so the settings UI can still show it as off. The wizard also stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening it shows stale codes. The user may never have saved the codes either. The dismiss path should be handled the same way as Close, or dismissal should be blocked on this step.

Copy button shows success toast without awaiting the clipboard write

`navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (permission denied, non-secure context, unfocused document), the user is told the codes were copied when they were not. For one-time recovery codes this is risky. Await the promise and show the toast only on success, with an error path otherwise.

Empty backup code submit silently does nothing on the login form

The login form uses `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the BackupCode input are not enforced. Submitting an empty backup code sends `backupCode: ""`, which is falsy. The server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`. The handler then just calls `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` (already true), with no error shown. The user sees nothing happen. Handle the empty case client-side or show an error.

No test coverage for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code

The core new behaviour is untested, and the PR checklist admits no tests were added. The e2e changes only click download/copy/close on the new screen, and the file/clipboard contents are TODOs. Nothing exercises backup-code login, one-time consumption of a code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, or the MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode paths. The first test ("enable and login") never closes the new backup-codes dialog. Its `isChecked()` assertion is always truthy, as the FIXME admits, so it does not verify the new step. Given that this is authentication code, tests for the login and disable paths should be included.

Unvalidated backupCode type can crash the disable endpoint

`req.body.backupCode` is only checked for truthiness, then `.replaceAll` is called on it. A non-string truthy value (number, object, array) throws a TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a 400 `IncorrectBackupCode`. Validate that it is a string before use, and ideally trim it.

tabIndex={-1} on the shared password visibility toggle removes it from keyboard navigation

This is a shared `PasswordField` used across the whole app, and the change makes the show/hide-password button unreachable by keyboard for every form. It is unrelated to backup codes and is an accessibility regression. If the goal was to improve tab order on the login or disable-2FA forms, apply it locally instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet

The second entry overwrites the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown? }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys by default.
